newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA says not heard from Bank Austria.
newsitem.headline: CA says not heard from Bank Austria.

text.p: Austria's Creditanstalt said on Monday it was still in the dark about the future plans of its new majority shareholder Bank Austria, one day after it was taken under the wing of its arch-rival.
"We still haven't heard from either Bank Austria or the government," a Creditanstalt spokesman told Reuters.

The merger was agreed by leaders of Austria's frayed Social Democrat-conservative government coalition after 11 hours of emergency talks over the weekend, pulling the government back from the brink of collapse over Europe's longest privatisation.

Bank Austria agreed to pay 17.2 billion schillings for the state's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt and offered to buy out the bank's minority shareholders in what it described as the "biggest step" in its history.
Creditanstalt supervisory board chairman Walter Fremuth on Monday offered to resign from his post and suggested the bank's executive board had to decide for itself whether to follow his lead.
According to the fine print agreed by the government leaders, Creditanstalt will remain an independent bank for at least five years.
Fremuth said the next five years would be a "test period" for both partners to see whether they could realise sufficient synergies together or each on his own.

"The most important thing now is to make sure that one plus one will be more than two," he told Austrian state radio. "If the synergies can be realised with the two banks remaining independent, maybe there won't be a fusion after five years."
Bank Austria has said the financial marriage would result in billions of schillings in extra revenue for the combined bank and help to double earnings per share over the next five years.

But Bank Austria was forced to give in to political pressure and give a job guarantee to all of Creditanstalt's 9,800 employees, saying job reductions would be achieved through natural attrition only. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
